_readme: Duplicate register ids a human has SEEN and owes a decision on. Default-deny: any
duplicate not listed here fails `node scripts/check-register-id-uniqueness.mjs`.
A waiver is NOT a resolution. It says only that the collision is known and that
renumbering needs a decision a guard cannot make. Every entry is reported on green
runs so it cannot be forgotten, and `stale_waiver` fires the moment the duplicate is
gone, so a waiver cannot outlive the defect it covers. Delete the entry in the same
commit that fixes the duplicate.
SHAPE: each entry needs THREE fields -- a non-empty `reason`; `occurrences`, an integer
>= 2 saying how many definitions the declarer looked at; and `identities`, the exact
source text of each of those occurrences. All three are enforced.
Keying a waiver on the id ALONE (the shape this file shipped with) made the waived id a
permanent blind spot: a THIRD unrelated definition was silently absorbed by the waiver
for the first two. `occurrences` closed that -- but a count catches only ADD and REMOVE,
so REPLACING either reviewed definition with a different one at another line still left
the count at 2 and the waiver still applied. Both gaps were found by external review.
`identities` closes the second: the waiver binds to WHAT was reviewed, not just how many.
Identity is the definition's SOURCE TEXT, deliberately not `file:line`. Line numbers
drift on every edit above them, so binding to those would red CI on unrelated changes --
the cry-wolf failure that gets a guard switched off -- while the text is stable under
drift and changes exactly when a definition is swapped.
Currently EMPTY, and that is the intended resting state. The one entry this file was
created for -- `decision:104`, two locked decisions sharing a number -- was resolved by
renumbering the agent-update-concurrency decision to #125, and the entry was removed in
that same commit. `stale_waiver` proved it was doing its job on the way out: with the
duplicate fixed and the entry still present, the guard refused (exit 1) until it was
deleted. The mechanism stays for the next collision that needs a human decision.
